facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is that trailing issuer-adjusted EBITDA still holds a one-time first-quarter inventory gain of USD 102 million; without it net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 3.61x rather than 3.51x. Trailing reported EBITDA is flattered by net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million, and the refinery segment contributed USD 238 million of adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter against USD 456 million across nine months, a pace that the first-quarter turnaround makes hard to extrapolate. The view would weaken if the Offen purchase was debt funded and earns little in its first year, or if inventory and refinery margins normalise; it would strengthen if the next quarterly report shows leverage near the current level after Offen is included. Basis: calculation C10; calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex991sunerq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 22, 40

severity Low; the action is to obtain the quarterly breakdown. - Cash taxes paid are stated for fiscal years only and not for the nine-month periods, so trailing cash taxes are not calculable; severity Low; the action is to obtain interim cash tax data. - Unused revolver availability at December 31, 2024 is not stated, so the 2024 liquidity point shows cash only; severity Low; the action is to obtain the 2024 annual report. - Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so the debt instrument table carries principal with one financing cost adjustment; debt by seniority at carrying value is therefore not stated and senior secured, senior unsecured and subordinated debt rows of the balance sheet are not supplied; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the indentures and debt note detail. - The rank and security of the GoZone Bonds and of lease-related financing obligations and other subsidiary debt are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack, covering USD 919 million of principal; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the governing agreements. - The margin in force on the Credit Facility and its reference rate for the Canadian dollar drawings are not stated; severity Low; the action is to obtain the credit agreement. - Offen Petroleum's earnings and the funding split between cash and revolver are not stated, so the pro forma net leverage excludes its EBITDA and may overstate the effect; severity High for the post-quarter view; the action is to obtain the issuer's Offen disclosure or the next quarterly report. - The maturity ladder at September 30, 2026 is built from note titles and treats the Credit Facility as maturing in 2030; USD 597 million has no stated maturity and the current maturities of USD 7 million are not placed in a year; severity Medium; the action is to obtain a dated schedule. - The covenant Net Leverage Ratio is reported at 4.03x and 3.5x but its definition, with acquisition pro forma effects and cash netting, is not reproducible from the sources, so a gap to the calculated ratios cannot be fully explained; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the credit agreement. - Maintenance and growth capital are stated only on an accrual basis for FY2025 and nine months 2026, not on a cash basis for other periods; severity Low; the action is to obtain a cash split.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Energy Transfer controls the borrower through its general partner, and the partnership agreement lets that general partner weigh Energy Transfer's interests against those of the partnership and its unitholders. Energy Transfer owns all of the general partner, 20.79% of the common units and every incentive distribution right, and its power to appoint the board runs through SunocoCorp under a delegation agreement. Five of the seven directors were independent at year-end 2025 and an independent audit committee oversees reporting, but the annual report describes no creditor vote, and the general partner alone decides borrowing, reserves, asset sales and whether spending counts as maintenance. Basis: calculation C01; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 92, 93, 155, 156, 193

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Related-party dealings are large in volume but small against cost of sales, and they rose sharply in 2026. Purchases of motor fuel from Energy Transfer affiliates were USD 1,249 million in FY2025, 5.57% of cost of sales, and USD 1,760 million in nine months 2026, 4.60% of cost of sales, while sales to affiliates reached USD 884 million against USD 15 million a year earlier. Reimbursements to the general partner were USD 43 million in FY2025 with no cap in the partnership agreement, so the exposure is leakage and pricing discipline rather than funding, and the pricing basis is not established. Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 195, 196, 256; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Distributions take a large and rising share of cash flow, but coverage is ample and growth is deliberate policy. Distributions paid were USD 880 million in nine months 2026, 39.09% of operating cash flow, and the third-quarter distribution per unit is 10.28% above a year earlier, the eighth consecutive increase against management's stated multi-year distribution growth rate of at least 5%. Adjusted distributable cash flow covered the USD 267 million third-quarter payout 2.20x, but incentive distribution rights take 28.46% of it, and the partnership agreement requires distribution of available cash, so growth capital and acquisitions rely mainly on external financing. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Acquisition appetite is high and recent funding mixed debt with equity-like claims. Since 2024 the group closed the NuStar, Parkland, TanQuid and Delta purchases, and the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million closed after the quarter. facts.text: The business is diversified but still earns about half its segment profit from motor fuel distribution. facts.text: Creditors rely on guarantees from only part of the group. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Exchange and domicile changes lighten outside governance checks. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a medium risk view is that equity-like funding carried the largest deal. Class D units valued at USD 2,547 million and USD 1.47 billion of preferred units went into Parkland, leverage on the issuer's own covenant basis fell from 4.03x at year-end 2025 to 3.5x at September 30, 2026, distributions are well covered and the board has a majority of independent directors. That would point to low risk if repeated, and it wins if the next acquisitions are equity funded and distribution growth is paced to deleveraging. The view would worsen if the Offen purchase was debt funded without deleveraging, if related-party sales keep growing from USD 884 million, or if the delegation agreement or the listing change were used to reduce creditor information or consent rights. Basis: calculation C02; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 197, 251; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 15

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: After Parkland the group completed TanQuid on 2026-01-16, with equity consideration of EUR 206 million and assumed debt of EUR 298 million, and Delta on 2026-04-01 for about USD 81 million, funded from cash and the Credit Facility. In March 2026 it issued USD 600 million of 5.375% notes due 2031 and USD 600 million of 5.625% notes due 2034 and used part of the proceeds to redeem USD 500 million of 2026 notes and USD 600 million of 2027 notes, then redeemed the remaining Parkland notes and, by August 2026, its Canadian-dollar notes. The Offen Petroleum acquisition, closed on 2026-10-27 for approximately USD 600 million in cash, is after the quarter end and not in any reported balance. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The first strength is earnings scale across four segments: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,889 million came 53.86% from fuel distribution, 18.52% from pipelines, 11.84% from terminals and 15.78% from the refinery, so no single segment decides debt service, which lowers the odds that one shock breaks leverage. The second is liquidity of USD 3,060 million, 23.25% of total debt, with no note maturing in 2026 and a revolver to 2030, which gives time to refinance the 2027 notes. The third is equity-like funding of the largest deal, with Class D units of USD 2,547 million and preferred units of USD 1.47 billion, which limited the debt added and supports the 3.5x covenant leverage. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 22

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Sunoco LP distributes motor fuel to about 11,000 branded and partner locations, owns about 14,000 miles of pipeline, over 170 terminals and a refinery in British Columbia, and operates in 33 countries and territories. Contract-based dealer and commission-agent supply, fee-based pipelines and terminals and a regulated tariff base give cash-flow visibility, but most revenue is fuel sold at pass-through prices, so earnings follow the margin per gallon, not revenue. The group grew by acquisition (NuStar in 2024, Parkland in 2025, then TanQuid, Delta and Offen), which adds scale and integration risk and raises debt service needs. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 11

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Energy Transfer owns the general partner, 20.8% of the common units and all incentive distribution rights, and appoints the board through SunocoCorp, which holds the Class D units. The general partner may favour its owner, has no cap on cost reimbursements and decides borrowing and distributions, so financial policy is the owner's to set; the independent audit committee and five independent directors out of seven are the checks. Debt is issued at Sunoco LP, Sunoco Finance Corp and NuStar Logistics with reciprocal subsidiary guarantees, and non-guarantor subsidiaries, including Parkland businesses, sit structurally ahead of the notes. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 92, 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 47, 48

facts.label: Porter's Five Forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense and margins are narrow in wholesale and retail fuel, so a competitor price move quickly compresses the per-gallon margin. New entrants face high asset costs in pipelines and terminals, while retail fuel already faces many competitors across store formats, which caps pricing in that part of the portfolio. Substitutes, mainly alternative fuels and efficiency gains, are a long-dated volume risk the annual report flags. Buyers have contract-bound volumes through dealers, which limits switching, and suppliers, with Chevron, Exxon, Phillips 66 and Valero the largest branded sources, hold bargaining power over supply and trade credit terms. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12, 16, 66

Buyers have contract-bound volumes through dealers, which limits switching, and suppliers, with Chevron, Exxon, Phillips 66 and Valero the largest branded sources, hold bargaining power over supply and trade credit terms.

facts.label: PEST
facts.text: Regulation and litigation are the material factors. The pipeline tariff index was reset in April 2026 to producer prices minus 0.55% for five years from July 2026, which slows regulated pipeline revenue growth; Sunoco and an affiliate face climate-change lawsuits in several states with no loss estimate; foreign currency exposure produced a loss of USD 94 million in nine months 2026; and variable-rate debt of USD 398 million is exposed to rate moves of about USD 4 million a year per 100 bp. Other political, social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the documents read. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 30, 48, 50

facts.label: SWOT
facts.text: Strengths are the diversified segment base, the liquidity and maturity runway, and equity-like funding of Parkland. Weaknesses are acquisition-driven earnings, inventory-timing gains, the controller's policy discretion and structural subordination. Opportunities are integration benefits, with management expecting 2026 Adjusted EBITDA above its range, and refinancing the 2027 notes at longer maturity. Threats are margin compression, an Offen purchase that earns little, tariff pressure on pipelines and climate or tax disputes. facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over twelve to twenty-four months the supportive items are a full year of Parkland, management guidance above its USD 3.5 billion to USD 3.7 billion range and planned growth spending that can be trimmed; the pressures are the Offen purchase, 2027 and 2028 refinancing of USD 1,949 million and inventory timing that reverses. Over three to five years the pipeline tariff index, fuel demand and the integration of a larger Canadian and Caribbean footprint decide whether leverage settles near the current level. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with the fuel margin falling from 16.9 cents per gallon in nine months 2026 to the 13.2 cents of FY2025, a drop of 3.7 cents. On trailing volume of 15,432 million gallons, each cent per gallon is worth about USD 154.3 million of EBITDA, so the drop removes USD 571 million, 16.15% of adjusted EBITDA. Trailing adjusted EBITDA falls to USD 2,964 million, net debt to EBITDA rises from 3.51x to 4.18x, or 4.39x if the Offen purchase is added without earnings, and cash interest cover falls to 4.08x. Free cash flow falls to about USD 1,334 million before tax effects, still above distributions of USD 1,049 million, so liquidity of USD 3,060 million covers the 2027 and 2028 notes without distress, but deleveraging stalls and management's levers are growth spending and the pace of distributions. Basis: calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Sunoco LP presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, segment diversification and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that rely on acquisitions and inventory timing, a controlling owner's policy discretion and structural subordination. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers distributions, though not with a wide margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding leverage near 3.51x through the Offen integration and on market access for the 2027 notes. The primary downside path is margin compression with a debt-funded acquisition, and further analysis would need a rating, the credit agreement and Offen's earnings. Top risk: margin compression while distributions and acquisition funding continue. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven Sunoco LP sources support a credit snapshot as of 2026-11-05, but only on the issuer's own debt summaries, because no credit agreement, indenture, rating or market price was supplied. Covenant headroom, legal priority and relative value therefore cannot be verified here, and any conclusion on them rests on the filings' descriptions.

The latest balance sheet is also not the current position. The all-cash purchase of Offen Petroleum for approximately USD 600 million closed on 2026-10-27, after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date, so quarter-end debt, leverage and liquidity exclude it, and how it was funded is not established. Quarterly and nine-month 2025 comparatives contain none of Parkland, which closed on 2025-10-31, so growth against them mixes acquisition effects with underlying change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for Sunoco LP (issuer id sun) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is Sunoco LP consolidated statements for FY2024, FY2025, nine months and the third quarter of 2026 against 2025, carrying-value debt, liquidity, the maturity ladder, derived trailing figures and the events after September 30, 2026 that the sources state.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-19 | 4d533c7220ddbcba5e79429a3e55af6f981f4028bd3240e90c171b5489b87bbb | Audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements, segment note, debt note, maturity schedule, Credit Facility and covenant summary, interest and tax paid. |

| EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the third quarter of 2026, covering Sunoco LP and SunocoCorp LLC | 2026-11-03 | 9cda190739e5a6207ea6c7ec1f929f6d3b9334edb87da0e79d1dca3af0892d56 | Cross-check of Adjusted EBITDA, reported net leverage and revolver liquidity; Sunoco LP pages only. |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sunoco LP's net debt was USD 12,403 million at September 30, 2026, or 3.51x trailing issuer-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves creditors with moderate leverage and ample interest cover, but the roughly USD 600 million Offen purchase that closed after the quarter already raises it.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

The fall from the 6.11x of year-end 2025 is mostly a comparison effect, because that year held only two months of Parkland earnings against a full balance sheet, and the issuer's own covenant ratio was 4.03x. Trailing adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 4.87x, and trailing reported EBITDA of USD 3,624 million includes net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million that adjusted EBITDA removes.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 251; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 22
### Key findings

Net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 5.07x at year-end 2024, 6.11x at year-end 2025 and 3.51x at September 30, 2026, and on calculated reported EBITDA 3.42x at the latest date. The year-end 2025 jump came from carrying the debt of the Parkland acquisition against EBITDA that held two months of it. The 2026 fall came from the trailing figure holding about eleven months of Parkland, while carrying-value debt moved only from USD 13,389 million to USD 13,163 million.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 247

Cash interest paid over the trailing year was USD 726 million, so adjusted EBITDA covers it 4.87x and reported EBITDA 4.99x; after total capital expenditure of USD 738 million the cover is 3.98x on reported EBITDA. Cover was 4.72x on adjusted EBITDA in FY2025 and 4.30x in FY2024, so it has edged up from FY2025 and is above FY2024, with both resting on acquired earnings.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 243; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11

Operating cash flow of USD 2,251 million in the first nine months of 2026 included a USD 316 million working-capital release, so operating cash flow before working capital of USD 1,935 million is the cleaner anchor. After capital expenditure of USD 579 million, free cash flow was USD 1,672 million, against distributions of USD 880 million to common, Class D and preferred unitholders and USD 356 million paid for acquisitions.
Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 6

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 760 million of cash plus USD 2,300 million of unused revolver, or USD 3,060 million, which is 23.25% of total debt. The revolver matures in June 2030, and USD 1,049 million of 2027 notes are classified as long-term only because management intends to refinance them.
Basis: calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15

Senior unsecured notes make up USD 12,213 million of USD 13,243 million of principal, so the drawn revolver of USD 111 million is the only debt stated as secured, and the structure leans on subsidiary guarantees and equal-ranking unsecured claims. Maturities run USD 1,049 million in 2027, USD 900 million in 2028 and USD 2,723 million in 2029.
Basis: calculation C08; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 249, 250; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 14

Two events after the quarter are stated but not in any period figure: the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million, closed on 2026-10-27, and the third-quarter distribution of USD 267 million payable on 2026-11-19. Net debt alone after each would be USD 13,003 million (3.59x reported EBITDA) and USD 12,670 million (3.50x). How Offen was funded and what it earns are not established.
Basis: calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that trailing issuer-adjusted EBITDA still holds a one-time first-quarter inventory gain of USD 102 million; without it net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 3.61x rather than 3.51x. Trailing reported EBITDA is flattered by net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million, and the refinery segment contributed USD 238 million of adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter against USD 456 million across nine months, a pace that the first-quarter turnaround makes hard to extrapolate. The view would weaken if the Offen purchase was debt funded and earns little in its first year, or if inventory and refinery margins normalise; it would strengthen if the next quarterly report shows leverage near the current level after Offen is included.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex991sunerq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 22, 40
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is not stated by the issuer; it is calculated here as net income plus income tax, net interest and depreciation, amortization and accretion, and the issuer's only EBITDA measure is its adjusted one.
Basis: calculation C01; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22
- Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so the debt instrument table and debt stack use principal, with one reconciling financing-cost line to carrying value.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 14

- The maturity ladder at September 30, 2026 is built from the maturity year in each note's title, because the quarterly report prints no schedule; USD 597 million of lease-related and other subsidiary debt has no stated maturity.
Basis: calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13
- The rank of the GoZone Bonds and of lease-related financing obligations is not stated, so they are outside the debt stack.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 14
- Offen's earnings and funding are not stated, so no pro forma leverage includes its EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10
- Year-end 2025 ratios are not comparable with the trailing figure, because FY2025 holds two months of Parkland.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7

## Gaps

- The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA for every period is calculated from net income, income tax, net interest and depreciation, amortization and accretion; this restricts any ratio on a reported basis to a calculated denominator; severity Medium; the action is to confirm the definition with the issuer or a lender presentation.

- Several statement lines print a dash or have no line in some reports (the West Texas Sale in 2025 and 2026, the preferred and Class D allocations before September 2025, acquisition and financing lines in other periods, accounts receivable from affiliates before 2026, and refinery operating data before the acquisition); these are shown as not supplied rather than zero; severity Low; no action is needed.

- The interim reports do not break net interest expense into gross interest, financing fee amortization and interest income, which the annual report gives for fiscal years only, and they print cash flow on a year-to-date basis, so third-quarter 2026 cash flow and cash interest were not constructed; severity Low; the action is to obtain the quarterly breakdown.
- Cash taxes paid are stated for fiscal years only and not for the nine-month periods, so trailing cash taxes are not calculable; severity Low; the action is to obtain interim cash tax data.
- Unused revolver availability at December 31, 2024 is not stated, so the 2024 liquidity point shows cash only; severity Low; the action is to obtain the 2024 annual report.

- Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so the debt instrument table carries principal with one financing cost adjustment; debt by seniority at carrying value is therefore not stated and senior secured, senior unsecured and subordinated debt rows of the balance sheet are not supplied; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the indentures and debt note detail.

- The rank and security of the GoZone Bonds and of lease-related financing obligations and other subsidiary debt are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack, covering USD 919 million of principal; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the governing agreements.
- The margin in force on the Credit Facility and its reference rate for the Canadian dollar drawings are not stated; severity Low; the action is to obtain the credit agreement.

- Offen Petroleum's earnings and the funding split between cash and revolver are not stated, so the pro forma net leverage excludes its EBITDA and may overstate the effect; severity High for the post-quarter view; the action is to obtain the issuer's Offen disclosure or the next quarterly report.

- The maturity ladder at September 30, 2026 is built from note titles and treats the Credit Facility as maturing in 2030; USD 597 million has no stated maturity and the current maturities of USD 7 million are not placed in a year; severity Medium; the action is to obtain a dated schedule.

- The covenant Net Leverage Ratio is reported at 4.03x and 3.5x but its definition, with acquisition pro forma effects and cash netting, is not reproducible from the sources, so a gap to the calculated ratios cannot be fully explained; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the credit agreement.
- Maintenance and growth capital are stated only on an accrual basis for FY2025 and nine months 2026, not on a cash basis for other periods; severity Low; the action is to obtain a cash split.

spans.text: ## Request

Business & governance for Sunoco LP (issuer id sun) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and sponsor behaviour, transactions and capitalisation, and dated issuer history that the supplied annual report, quarterly reports and earnings releases support.
## Sources

No external source was used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Sunoco LP's creditors face medium governance and structure risk: an Energy Transfer-controlled general partner holds broad discretion over borrowing, distributions and acquisitions, while the notes are guaranteed by only part of a group that earns nearly half its profit outside the guarantor perimeter.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 92, 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 47, 48; calculation C09

The business itself is diversified and fee-supported: fuel distribution earned about 53.86% of nine-month 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA, with pipelines, terminals and the acquired refinery supplying the rest. Distributions have risen eight quarters in a row and the third-quarter payout was covered 2.20x by adjusted distributable cash flow, and recent acquisitions were funded partly with preferred and Class D units rather than debt alone, which tempers the risk.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 22; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 7
### Key findings

Energy Transfer controls the borrower through its general partner, and the partnership agreement lets that general partner weigh Energy Transfer's interests against those of the partnership and its unitholders. Energy Transfer owns all of the general partner, 20.79% of the common units and every incentive distribution right, and its power to appoint the board runs through SunocoCorp under a delegation agreement. Five of the seven directors were independent at year-end 2025 and an independent audit committee oversees reporting, but the annual report describes no creditor vote, and the general partner alone decides borrowing, reserves, asset sales and whether spending counts as maintenance.
Basis: calculation C01; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 92, 93, 155, 156, 193

Related-party dealings are large in volume but small against cost of sales, and they rose sharply in 2026. Purchases of motor fuel from Energy Transfer affiliates were USD 1,249 million in FY2025, 5.57% of cost of sales, and USD 1,760 million in nine months 2026, 4.60% of cost of sales, while sales to affiliates reached USD 884 million against USD 15 million a year earlier. Reimbursements to the general partner were USD 43 million in FY2025 with no cap in the partnership agreement, so the exposure is leakage and pricing discipline rather than funding, and the pricing basis is not established.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 195, 196, 256; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Distributions take a large and rising share of cash flow, but coverage is ample and growth is deliberate policy. Distributions paid were USD 880 million in nine months 2026, 39.09% of operating cash flow, and the third-quarter distribution per unit is 10.28% above a year earlier, the eighth consecutive increase against management's stated multi-year distribution growth rate of at least 5%. Adjusted distributable cash flow covered the USD 267 million third-quarter payout 2.20x, but incentive distribution rights take 28.46% of it, and the partnership agreement requires distribution of available cash, so growth capital and acquisitions rely mainly on external financing.

Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 122; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 6, 20; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 7

Acquisition appetite is high and recent funding mixed debt with equity-like claims. Since 2024 the group closed the NuStar, Parkland, TanQuid and Delta purchases, and the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million closed after the quarter. Parkland was paid for with cash and Class D units issued to SunocoCorp, the cash raised through USD 1.9 billion of new senior notes and USD 1.47 billion of Series A preferred units, which keeps part of the burden outside debt but adds preferred distributions of about USD 118.1 million a year that rank ahead of common units. Management says leverage returned to its target in less than one year, but the target level is not stated.

Basis: calculation C02; calculation C07; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8, 249; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 20; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2

The business is diversified but still earns about half its segment profit from motor fuel distribution. In nine months 2026 fuel distribution produced 53.86% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, pipelines 18.52%, terminals 11.84% and the refinery 15.78%, and the refinery's quarterly Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 43 million in the first quarter of 2026, hit by a turnaround, to USD 175 million and then USD 238 million. Contractually committed revenue of USD 2,038 million at September 30, 2026 gives some visibility, and 89.26% of FY2025 revenue was in the United States before a full year of Parkland's Canadian and Caribbean operations.

Basis: calculation C06; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 258, 279; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex991sunerq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_ex991sunerq22026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Creditors rely on guarantees from only part of the group. In nine months 2026 the guarantor issuer group had USD 22,894 million of revenue and USD 758 million of net income, against USD 20,080 million and USD 667 million for the non-guarantor subsidiaries, whose long-term assets were USD 11,730 million; the notes are structurally subordinated to the non-guarantors' debts. Before USD 5,510 million of investments in non-guarantors, the guarantor group's liabilities exceeded its assets by USD 2,031 million, so note holders depend on the value of those subsidiaries.
Basis: calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 47, 48

Exchange and domicile changes lighten outside governance checks. Sunoco converted from a Delaware to a Texas limited partnership under a plan dated 2026-07-02, and its units are now listed on the Texas Stock Exchange, which does not require a majority-independent board or compensation and nominating committees for a partnership; the general partner's own agreement still requires at least three independent directors.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a medium risk view is that equity-like funding carried the largest deal. Class D units valued at USD 2,547 million and USD 1.47 billion of preferred units went into Parkland, leverage on the issuer's own covenant basis fell from 4.03x at year-end 2025 to 3.5x at September 30, 2026, distributions are well covered and the board has a majority of independent directors. That would point to low risk if repeated, and it wins if the next acquisitions are equity funded and distribution growth is paced to deleveraging.

The view would worsen if the Offen purchase was debt funded without deleveraging, if related-party sales keep growing from USD 884 million, or if the delegation agreement or the listing change were used to reduce creditor information or consent rights.

### Limitations

- The partnership agreement, delegation agreement, omnibus agreement, credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the conclusion that the general partner holds broad discretion rests on the annual report's summaries and could prove narrower or wider in the documents themselves.

- Energy Transfer's share of SunocoCorp's economics is not stated, so the sponsor's total economic interest in the borrower is not established and the control conclusion rests on legal rights rather than on economic exposure.

- Customer concentration, a rating and the pricing basis of related-party fuel trade are not stated, so the diversification conclusion cannot be tested against a top-customer share and the leakage reading cannot be priced.
- Offen's earnings and funding are not stated, so the acquisition-appetite conclusion covers the funding mix of earlier deals only, and the use of the 2024 asset-sale proceeds is not stated.
- Management's leverage target is not quantified, so the statement that leverage returned to target cannot be checked and the leverage view rests on the covenant ratio alone.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The defining transaction is the Parkland acquisition, which closed on 2025-10-31: Sunoco paid Parkland shareholders cash and issued Class D units to SunocoCorp, whose units were exchanged for Parkland shares, and it assumed or exchanged about USD 3.65 billion of Parkland debt into its own notes. The financing before closing was USD 1.0 billion of 5.625% notes due 2031 and USD 900 million of 5.875% notes due 2034 in September 2025, alongside 1.5 million 7.875% Series A preferred units with net proceeds of about USD 1.47 billion.

After Parkland the group completed TanQuid on 2026-01-16, with equity consideration of EUR 206 million and assumed debt of EUR 298 million, and Delta on 2026-04-01 for about USD 81 million, funded from cash and the Credit Facility. In March 2026 it issued USD 600 million of 5.375% notes due 2031 and USD 600 million of 5.625% notes due 2034 and used part of the proceeds to redeem USD 500 million of 2026 notes and USD 600 million of 2027 notes, then redeemed the remaining Parkland notes and, by August 2026, its Canadian-dollar notes. The Offen Petroleum acquisition, closed on 2026-10-27 for approximately USD 600 million in cash, is after the quarter end and not in any reported balance.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10, 14; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex991sunerq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2

The registrant also converted from a Delaware to a Texas limited partnership, with the Plan of Conversion dated 2026-07-02, and moved its listing to the Texas Stock Exchange; the related current report and the new partnership agreement are not in the documents supplied.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sunoco LP is an adequate, moderately leveraged credit: liquidity of USD 3,060 million and a diversified earnings base support it, while leverage that rests on acquired earnings and a controlling owner's discretion limits headroom.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06

Net debt was USD 12,403 million at September 30, 2026, 3.51x trailing adjusted EBITDA, and USD 13,003 million pro forma for the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million that closed on 2026-10-27; cash interest is covered 4.87x. Distributions absorb much of free cash flow, so leverage falls only if earnings hold. The primary downside path is a fall in fuel margins to the 2025 level, which would lift leverage to 4.18x without threatening liquidity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C05
### Key findings

Scale and diversification support the profile, but earnings quality is flattered. Fuel distribution, pipelines, terminals and the refinery all contribute, with fuel distribution about half of segment Adjusted EBITDA, yet trailing reported EBITDA of USD 3,624 million holds net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million and adjusted EBITDA holds a one-time first-quarter gain of USD 102 million; removing that gain lifts net leverage from 3.51x to 3.61x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02

Leverage is moderate and falling, but the fall is earnings-driven rather than repayment-driven. Net debt moved by only USD 95 million from year-end 2025 while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 1,488 million, and free cash flow after distributions was USD 856 million over the trailing year, 6.90% of net debt, so lower leverage depends on holding the acquired earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05

Liquidity covers the nearest maturities with room to spare. Cash and unused revolver of USD 3,060 million are 1.57x the USD 1,949 million of notes due in 2027 and 2028, the revolver runs to June 2030, and the largest maturity is USD 2,723 million in 2029. The 2027 notes are classified as long-term only because management intends to refinance them, and availability after the Offen purchase is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15

Acquisitions and distributions are the main policy risks. The Offen purchase raises net debt to USD 13,003 million, 3.59x calculated reported EBITDA, before any Offen earnings, and the partnership agreement requires distribution of available cash, so growth leans on external funding; governance risk is medium because a controlling owner holds broad discretion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C09

The structure ranks the secured revolver ahead of equal-ranking unsecured notes, and note holders depend on subsidiaries outside the guarantee. Senior unsecured notes are 92.22% of principal and the secured revolver 0.84%, while non-guarantor subsidiaries earned 46.77% of nine-month net income and the guarantor group's liabilities exceed its assets before investments in them.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger credit is that leverage on the issuer's own covenant basis fell from 4.03x at year-end 2025 to 3.5x at September 30, 2026, management expects 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to exceed its raised guidance range of USD 3.5 billion to USD 3.7 billion, and Parkland was funded partly with equity-like units. If the next quarter shows leverage at or below the current level after Offen, with distributions held within coverage, the view would move toward strong.

The strongest evidence for a weaker credit is that the improvement rests on one year of acquired earnings and inventory gains. If fuel margins revert to the 2025 level while Offen is debt funded, leverage reaches 4.39x on the calculated basis, and the view would weaken if distributions continue to grow faster than cash retained for repayment.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 251; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Limitations

- No agency rating, bond price or spread was supplied, so the conclusion that market access is adequate rests on issuance history alone and could change if investors price the 2027 refinancing wider than the 2026 notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

- The downside scenario moves one driver, the fuel margin, on reported margins and volumes, so it understates a combined shock with refinery or inventory effects and does not test Offen earning nothing.
Basis: calculation C04

- The credit agreement is not supplied and the issuer's covenant leverage differs from the figure calculated here, so the conclusion that leverage is moderate rests on the calculated basis and does not establish covenant headroom.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 251
- No sector data or peer set was supplied, so the business profile is not compared with typical leveraged issuers and the competitive-advantage judgement rests on the issuer's own descriptions.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The first strength is earnings scale across four segments: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,889 million came 53.86% from fuel distribution, 18.52% from pipelines, 11.84% from terminals and 15.78% from the refinery, so no single segment decides debt service, which lowers the odds that one shock breaks leverage. The second is liquidity of USD 3,060 million, 23.25% of total debt, with no note maturing in 2026 and a revolver to 2030, which gives time to refinance the 2027 notes. The third is equity-like funding of the largest deal, with Class D units of USD 2,547 million and preferred units of USD 1.47 billion, which limited the debt added and supports the 3.5x covenant leverage.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 22

Weaknesses. The first weakness is dependence on acquired and inventory-driven earnings: the trailing figures hold net inventory gains of USD 258 million and a one-time gain of USD 102 million, so the ratio can rise quickly if margins revert. The second is policy risk from the controller: distributions of USD 880 million in nine months, a distribution growth aim of at least 5%, incentive distribution rights taking 28.46% of the third-quarter payout and the Offen purchase after the quarter. The third is structure: note holders depend on subsidiaries that earned 46.77% of net income but do not guarantee, and the rank of the GoZone Bonds and lease-related debt is not stated. The fourth is a lumpy maturity profile with USD 2,723 million due in 2029 and USD 1,949 million in 2027 and 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C07
### Company description

Sunoco LP distributes motor fuel to about 11,000 branded and partner locations, owns about 14,000 miles of pipeline, over 170 terminals and a refinery in British Columbia, and operates in 33 countries and territories. Contract-based dealer and commission-agent supply, fee-based pipelines and terminals and a regulated tariff base give cash-flow visibility, but most revenue is fuel sold at pass-through prices, so earnings follow the margin per gallon, not revenue. The group grew by acquisition (NuStar in 2024, Parkland in 2025, then TanQuid, Delta and Offen), which adds scale and integration risk and raises debt service needs.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 11
### Ownership and group structure

Energy Transfer owns the general partner, 20.8% of the common units and all incentive distribution rights, and appoints the board through SunocoCorp, which holds the Class D units. The general partner may favour its owner, has no cap on cost reimbursements and decides borrowing and distributions, so financial policy is the owner's to set; the independent audit committee and five independent directors out of seven are the checks. Debt is issued at Sunoco LP, Sunoco Finance Corp and NuStar Logistics with reciprocal subsidiary guarantees, and non-guarantor subsidiaries, including Parkland businesses, sit structurally ahead of the notes.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 92, 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 47, 48
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is mainly fuel sold at market-linked prices: fuel was 95.54% of third-quarter revenue, so the revenue line says little about credit quality and the margin per gallon, 16.9 cents in nine months 2026 against 10.9 cents a year earlier, matters most. Long-term dealer contracts and branded supply agreements give volume visibility, while commodity price swings, a shift to alternative fuels and supplier dependence limit pricing power. Contractually committed revenue is USD 2,038 million at September 30, 2026, small against fuel revenue.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 11
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are mostly pass-through fuel cost, with operating, lease and administrative costs of USD 1,664 million in nine months 2026 against USD 644 million a year earlier after Parkland. Margin resilience therefore depends on gross profit per gallon and on volume, not on cutting costs, and the first-quarter inventory gain and net inventory valuation gains show how timing effects move reported earnings. The group can defend margins in a volume dip through branded supply contracts, but not against a sharp margin compression.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex991sunerq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Free cash flow was USD 1,905 million over the trailing year after capital expenditure of USD 738 million, and about USD 1,049 million of distributions leave USD 856 million before acquisitions. Maintenance capital spending of USD 400 million to USD 450 million and growth capital of at least USD 600 million are planned for 2026, so growth spending is the flexible lever if liquidity tightens. Cash interest of USD 726 million takes 20.54% of trailing adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow benefited from a USD 316 million working-capital release in nine months 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 44
### Porter's Five Forces

Rivalry is intense and margins are narrow in wholesale and retail fuel, so a competitor price move quickly compresses the per-gallon margin. New entrants face high asset costs in pipelines and terminals, while retail fuel already faces many competitors across store formats, which caps pricing in that part of the portfolio. Substitutes, mainly alternative fuels and efficiency gains, are a long-dated volume risk the annual report flags. Buyers have contract-bound volumes through dealers, which limits switching, and suppliers, with Chevron, Exxon, Phillips 66 and Valero the largest branded sources, hold bargaining power over supply and trade credit terms.
### PEST

Regulation and litigation are the material factors. The pipeline tariff index was reset in April 2026 to producer prices minus 0.55% for five years from July 2026, which slows regulated pipeline revenue growth; Sunoco and an affiliate face climate-change lawsuits in several states with no loss estimate; foreign currency exposure produced a loss of USD 94 million in nine months 2026; and variable-rate debt of USD 398 million is exposed to rate moves of about USD 4 million a year per 100 bp. Other political, social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the documents read.
### SWOT

Strengths are the diversified segment base, the liquidity and maturity runway, and equity-like funding of Parkland. Weaknesses are acquisition-driven earnings, inventory-timing gains, the controller's policy discretion and structural subordination. Opportunities are integration benefits, with management expecting 2026 Adjusted EBITDA above its range, and refinancing the 2027 notes at longer maturity. Threats are margin compression, an Offen purchase that earns little, tariff pressure on pipelines and climate or tax disputes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 30
### Outlook

Over twelve to twenty-four months the supportive items are a full year of Parkland, management guidance above its USD 3.5 billion to USD 3.7 billion range and planned growth spending that can be trimmed; the pressures are the Offen purchase, 2027 and 2028 refinancing of USD 1,949 million and inventory timing that reverses. Over three to five years the pipeline tariff index, fuel demand and the integration of a larger Canadian and Caribbean footprint decide whether leverage settles near the current level. The documents do not state a leverage target, so the direction of deleveraging is not established.
Basis: calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_ex991sunerq22026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 30
### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with the fuel margin falling from 16.9 cents per gallon in nine months 2026 to the 13.2 cents of FY2025, a drop of 3.7 cents. On trailing volume of 15,432 million gallons, each cent per gallon is worth about USD 154.3 million of EBITDA, so the drop removes USD 571 million, 16.15% of adjusted EBITDA. Trailing adjusted EBITDA falls to USD 2,964 million, net debt to EBITDA rises from 3.51x to 4.18x, or 4.39x if the Offen purchase is added without earnings, and cash interest cover falls to 4.08x. Free cash flow falls to about USD 1,334 million before tax effects, still above distributions of USD 1,049 million, so liquidity of USD 3,060 million covers the 2027 and 2028 notes without distress, but deleveraging stalls and management's levers are growth spending and the pace of distributions.
Basis: calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132
### Overall credit view

Overall, Sunoco LP presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, segment diversification and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that rely on acquisitions and inventory timing, a controlling owner's policy discretion and structural subordination. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers distributions, though not with a wide margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding leverage near 3.51x through the Offen integration and on market access for the 2027 notes. The primary downside path is margin compression with a debt-funded acquisition, and further analysis would need a rating, the credit agreement and Offen's earnings. Top risk: margin compression while distributions and acquisition funding continue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04
